copy.about: induction and copying: the passage is re-typing something it already contains

conditions.repeat/prose: copy/induction in prose: fires on a word that already appeared earlier in the passage, not on the same word seen for the first time
conditions.piece/prose: copy in prose: fires on a later piece of a multi-piece word or name already seen earlier in the passage (the second mention), not on the same piece in a first mention
conditions.trigram/prose: copy in prose: fires deep inside a repeated string, where the last three tokens repeat an earlier three-token sequence, not on the same token where nothing repeats
conditions.repeat/code: copy/induction in code: fires on a word that already appeared earlier in the passage, not on the same word seen for the first time
conditions.piece/code: copy in code: fires on a later piece of a multi-piece word or name already seen earlier in the passage (the second mention), not on the same piece in a first mention
conditions.trigram/code: copy in code: fires deep inside a repeated string, where the last three tokens repeat an earlier three-token sequence, not on the same token where nothing repeats

conditions.topic/religion: topic: fires on ordinary words inside a passage about religion, not on the same words in English text on other subjects
conditions.topic/war: topic: fires on ordinary words inside a passage about war, not on the same words in English text on other subjects
conditions.topic/music: topic: fires on ordinary words inside a passage about music, not on the same words in English text on other subjects
conditions.topic/biology: topic: fires on ordinary words inside a passage about biology, not on the same words in English text on other subjects

conditions.lang/fr: language: fires inside fr text, not inside English or other Latin-script languages
conditions.lang/de: language: fires inside de text, not inside English or other Latin-script languages
conditions.lang/pt: language: fires inside pt text, not inside English or other Latin-script languages
conditions.lang/it: language: fires inside it text, not inside English or other Latin-script languages
conditions.lang/nl: language: fires inside nl text, not inside English or other Latin-script languages

conditions.script/cyrillic: script: fires inside cyrillic-script text, not inside Latin-script or other-script text
conditions.script/cjk: script: fires inside cjk-script text, not inside Latin-script or other-script text
conditions.script/arabic: script: fires inside arabic-script text, not inside Latin-script or other-script text
conditions.script/greek: script: fires inside greek-script text, not inside Latin-script or other-script text
conditions.script/hebrew: script: fires inside hebrew-script text, not inside Latin-script or other-script text

struct.about: structure: where in the code or document the current word sits (string, comment, nesting, indentation, list, heading)

conditions.code/in-string: structure: fires on a word inside a string literal in code, not on the same word in code outside strings
conditions.code/in-comment: structure: fires on a word inside a code comment, not on the same word in code
conditions.code/nested: structure: fires on a word nested two or more brackets deep in code, not on the same word at depth 0
conditions.code/indented: structure: fires on a word on a code line indented 8 or more spaces, not on the same word on an unindented line
conditions.prose/in-parens: structure: fires on a word inside parentheses in prose, not on the same word outside them
conditions.prose/in-quote: structure: fires on a word inside a quotation in prose, not on the same word in unquoted text
conditions.prose/list-item: structure: fires on a word in a list item (a line starting with -, * or 1.), not on the same word in ordinary lines
conditions.prose/heading: structure: fires on a word in a markdown heading (a line starting with #), not on the same word in body text

number.about: numbers: which digit of a number this is, and what kind of number (year, decimal, price)

conditions.num/digit1: number: fires on the first digit of a number, not on the same digit elsewhere in a number
conditions.num/digit2: number: fires on the second digit of a number, not on the same digit elsewhere in a number
conditions.num/digit3: number: fires on the third digit of a number, not on the same digit elsewhere in a number
conditions.num/digit4: number: fires on the fourth digit of a number, not on the same digit elsewhere in a number
conditions.num/year: number: fires on the last digit of a year (1500-2099), not on the fourth digit of other numbers
conditions.num/decimal: number: fires on a digit after a decimal point, not on the same digit in a whole number
conditions.num/currency: number: fires on a digit of an amount after a currency sign ($, €, £, ¥), not on the same digit in other numbers

predict.about:
Prediction neurons: found from the weights (an inverse analysis of the output side), tested on the model's own predictions.

1. Direct effect. For each pole, W_U · (final-norm gain ⊙ W_down[:, n]) · sign gives the 20 tokens it promotes most (its
   set S) and its spike: how far the 20th token stands above the vocabulary mean, in standard deviations.
2. Selector (CPU). Take the pole's 32 strongest corpus activations from the scan and count how many are followed by a
   token in S. A pole is a candidate when at least 8 of 32 are, at 10 times or more the rate S's tokens occur in the
   corpus. At most CAP per layer, ranked by that count. The tested set is the tokens of S that follow those activations at
   least twice (at most SEEN_MAX, most frequent first): what the pole promotes and is seen to precede.
3. Test construction (GPU, logits only, no neuron is read). Candidate snippets come from the test split: 24 where the
   corpus continues with a token in S, and 16 that end on the same tokens but continue otherwise. The pole's own top
   windows are excluded. The model reads each snippet after the first preamble. (S below is the tested set.)
     - fire: the model puts at least 0.5 of its next-token probability on S;
     - quiet: the model puts at most 0.05 on S, ending on the same token as a fire snippet when one exists.
   So the near miss keeps the current word and differs only in what the model expects next.

read: last token, mean over the 3 PREAMBLES
placebo: per condition: selection on quiet-vs-quiet pairs (false selections) and an 8 + 8 quiet-vs-quiet test on the selected poles (false holds)
